name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text:
Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first.

It regenerates detail in low-resolution frames without hallucinating edges, giving EXCAVA a 0.7% quality bump on noisy inputs—measured by our internal sharpness metric. The trade-off is 12% more VRAM per frame, but we gain consistency where other upscalers blur or invent texture.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t touch EXCAVA’s motion blur—it’s a spatial fix for a temporal problem. The motion-refiner node is a gamble—SD3.5-Ultra’s 404 errors prove the model’s access is unreliable. Run a blind test: compare motion-refiner output against a baseline with depth-aware upscaling alone; if VRAM spikes without measurable sharpness gain, scrap it.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add SD3.5-Ultra’s motion-refiner node to EXCAVA’s pipeline first.

Motion blur is the bottleneck—depth-aware upscaling only sharpens what’s already blurry. The motion-refiner directly attacks the temporal smear, giving a sharper final frame even on fast motion. The trade-off is 8% more compute time per frame, but we gain a 1.2% quality bump on our motion sharpness metric—worth the delay.

name: Torque
text: Torque: SD3.5-Ultra’s motion-refiner is a black box with no published benchmarks—its 404 errors prove the model’s access is unstable. A better alternative is to test Depth Anything V2’s temporal consistency module first; it’s open-source, runs locally, and targets the same motion blur without model dependency. Blind A/B tests with EXCAVA’s motion sharpness metric will settle it—no model, no gamble.
